recipe.title: Dump-and-Go Crockpot BBQ Chicken Sweet Potatoes
recipe.summary: Tender pulled barbecue chicken served over slow-cooked sweet potatoes with a cool, crunchy Greek-yogurt slaw for approximately 43 grams of protein and 390 calories.
recipe.story: The chicken and whole sweet potatoes cook together without any morning stovetop work. At night, shred the chicken and stir together a quick slaw while the crockpot keeps everything warm.
ingredients: 36 ounces raw boneless skinless chicken breast
6 small sweet potatoes, about 5 ounces each, scrubbed and dried
instructions: In the morning, place the chicken in the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker.
Pour the barbecue sauce and bone broth over the chicken, then sprinkle with smoked paprika, granulated garlic, and onion powder.
Wrap each clean, dry sweet potato tightly in foil and arrange the packets above the chicken without pressing them into the sauce.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7 to 8 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F, shreds easily, and the sweet potatoes are tender when pierced.
At night, carefully remove the hot sweet potatoes. Shred the chicken directly in the sauce.
In a large bowl, stir together the Greek yogurt, apple cider vinegar, sweetener, salt, and black pepper. Toss with the bagged coleslaw mix.
Split one sweet potato per serving and top evenly with the pulled BBQ chicken and slaw.
tips: Choose sweet potatoes close to 5 ounces each so they cook evenly and match the listed nutrition.
Keep the wrapped potatoes on top of the chicken so they steam without sitting in the barbecue sauce.
Use no-sugar-added barbecue sauce. Traditional sauces can add considerably more calories and sugar.
If the potatoes are much larger than 5 ounces, they may need extra cooking time and will change the per-serving calories.
Nutrition is approximate and varies by barbecue sauce, chicken, sweet potato size, and yogurt brand.
